theme: प्रकृति, अन्न, और कर्म का जीवन-चक्र / Nature, food, and the living cycle of action
context: Krishna deepens the same insight: the world is sustained by a mutual chain. Beings live through food, food grows through rain, rain comes through sacrifice, and sacrifice arises from human action. The point is not mere ritual; it is that human life is woven into a larger ecological and moral order that cannot be treated as purely private.
contextHindi: कृष्ण उसी विचार को और गहराई से समझा रहे हैं: दुनिया एक पारस्परिक चक्र से चलती है। जीव अन्न से रहते हैं, अन्न वर्षा से बनता है, वर्षा यज्ञ से होती है, और यज्ञ कर्म से उत्पन्न होता है। बात सिर्फ़ पूजा नहीं है; यह यह बताता है कि मानव जीवन एक बड़े जैविक और नैतिक क्रम से जुड़ा हुआ है, जिसे निजी चीज़ मानकर अलग नहीं किया जा सकता।
sanskritDevanagari:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः |
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ||३-१४||
transliteration:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ .
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ ||3-14||

wordByWord.meaning: from rain; from the rains that nourish the earth
the origin or production of food
sacrifice, offering, the harmonizing act of giving and receiving
born of action; from human effort and duty

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक जीवन के एक बड़े चक्र को बताता है। ‘अन्नात् भवन्ति भूतानि’—जीव अन्न से उत्पन्न होते हैं। यानी शरीर, ऊर्जा, विकास, सब कुछ भोजन से आता है। फिर ‘पर्जन्यात् अन्नसम्भवः’—वर्षा से अन्न का जन्म होता है। ‘यज्ञाद् भवति पर्जन्यः’—यज्ञ से वर्षा होती है। और ‘यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः’—यज्ञ कर्म से उत्पन्न होता है। यह क्रम समझाता है कि मानव जीवन अकेला नहीं है; वह प्रकृति, वातावरण, सामाजिक व्यवस्था और अपने कर्म के बीच एक जुड़ा हुआ तंत्र है। इसलिए भोजन को केवल ‘सिर्फ़ मेरी जरूरत’ मानना अंधापन है। एक व्यक्ति का कर्म, उसका काम, उसकी सच्ची निष्ठा, और उसका संबंध समूचे जीवन के साथ जुड़ा है।
clearEnglish: TEXT: The verse states a circular dependence: beings arise from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is born from action. This is a cosmological and ethical teaching about interdependence. The text is not offering a modern scientific model but a moral image of connected life: what we do, what the earth yields, and how the community nourishes itself belong to one process. INFERENCE: A person cannot remain isolated from the web of life. When action is reduced to personal gain, the whole flow of nourishment and reciprocity becomes distorted. The verse suggests that right living is not separate from ecology, gratitude, or duty. It is a reminder that human effort is part of a larger order, and the quality of that effort affects the whole chain—food, rain, health, and social harmony.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse explicitly names a chain: beings depend on food, food on rain, rain on sacrifice, and sacrifice on action. The language is concrete, cyclical, and relational rather than purely individualistic.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse supports the inference that human beings are not self-sufficient; ethical action participates in a larger order of giving, receiving, and sustaining life.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Many traditional readings stress that yajña represents a broader principle of harmonious contribution and cosmic reciprocity. That emphasis is helpful, but the verse itself teaches a pattern of interdependence rather than a narrow ritual formula.

practicalApplication.label: Respect the chain
practicalApplication.text: Notice where your food, water, and energy come from. A daily moment of gratitude for the people, land, and systems that sustain you reduces the illusion that life is produced by the self alone.

practicalApplication.label: Work as contribution
practicalApplication.text: Before starting work, ask: am I acting only for personal gain, or am I also contributing to the health of the people and world around me?

reflectionQuestion: In what ways do I live as if I were separate from the larger chain of food, labor, and care, and what would it look like to live with more reciprocity?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मैं अपने आप को भोजन, श्रम, और देखभाल के बड़े चक्र से अलग मानता हूँ—किस तरह? अधिक पारस्परिकता के साथ जीने का अर्थ क्या होगा?
